map.→ 打开社工（介入/评估/资源）链接工具: -> Open the social work (intervention / assessment / resource) linking tool
map.介入需求分几级？: How many levels of intervention need are there?
map.从 4 个维度（每项 0-3 分）评估老年人的社工介入需求并链接资源，输出需求等: Assesses the social work intervention needs of older people across 4 dimensions (each 0-3) and links resources, outputting a need level for community eldercare social work planning.
map.单维度评分≥2 视为重点介入，工具会据维度推送对应资源（如健康照护→长护险申请、: A single dimension scoring 2 or above counts as a priority intervention, and the tool pushes the matching resources per dimension (for example health care to long-term care insurance applications, social support to volunteer pairing), enabling targeted assistance.
map.居家养老服务中，按经济保障、健康照护、心理支持、社会支持四维度评估介入需求。: In home-based eldercare, assess intervention needs across four dimensions: economic security, health care, psychological support and social support.
map.本工具按四维度求和（满分 12）：≤3 低需求、≤7 中需求、>7 高需求。高需: This tool sums the four dimensions (maximum 12): 3 or below is low need, 7 or below medium need, above 7 high need. High need requires immediate case management and links to multiple resources.
map.社工（介入/评估/资源）链接 使用指南: Social work (intervention / assessment / resource) linking guide
map.算例：四项均评 0（状况良好）: Worked example: all four items scored 0 (condition good)
map.算例：四项均评 2（重点介入）: Worked example: all four items scored 2 (priority intervention)
map.评估结果为低/中/高需求，对应不同随访频次与资源链接策略。: A result of low, medium or high need maps to a different visit frequency and resource linking strategy.
map.重点维度（评分≥2）自动生成资源链接清单（如长护险、日间照料）。: Priority dimensions (scoring 2 or above) automatically generate a list of resource links (such as long-term care insurance and day care).
map.：介入需求总分 = 0 / 12 → 『低需求』，建议定期随访、保持社区联系即可: : an intervention need total of 0 / 12 gives "low need"; periodic follow-up and keeping community contact is enough.
map.：总分 = 8 > 7 → 『高需求』，立即个案管理、多专业协作、每周随访，并链: : a total of 8, which is above 7, gives "high need": start case management immediately, bring in multiple professions, follow up weekly, and link the four matching resources (means-tested benefit, family doctor, mental health hotline, day care and so on).
